permutationLabel: TG18 Grade I (mild) — only one Grade II criterion (age ≥75)
summary: 78-year-old man with 3 days of intermittent RUQ pain, fever 38.4 °C and jaundice; WBC 11.2, bilirubin 58 µmol/L, albumin 36, CBD 9 mm. One Grade II criterion (age) only, no organ dysfunction: TG18 Grade I.

inputs.hpi: Three days of intermittent right upper quadrant pain, fever and yellow eyes. Dark urine. Eating and drinking. No confusion.

exam.general: Mildly jaundiced, alert and orientated. Temperature 38.4°C, pulse 92/min, BP 138/80.
exam.abdomen: Mild right upper quadrant tenderness, no guarding, no palpable mass.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones. CBD dilated to 9 mm; distal duct obscured by bowel gas. No liver lesion.

inputs.socialHistory: Retired farmer. Lives with wife. Non-smoker.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute cholangitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Mild acute cholangitis secondary to presumed choledocholithiasis — TG18 Grade I (one Grade II criterion only: age ≥75). No organ dysfunction.

mustNotMiss.note: Painless-predominant jaundice in a 78-year-old: malignant biliary obstruction should stay on the differential until the distal duct is imaged.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 includes Inguinal / Femoral Hernia (male/age prior modifiers) instead.

emergencyLevel.note: Even mild cholangitis needs admission, antibiotics and a drainage plan if no response within 24 h.

mustNotAlarm.note: Normal heart rate, BP and mentation ('No confusion' is a pertinent negative). A sepsis banner here is caused by negation handling, not physiology.
mustNotAlarm.knownGapNote: iOS ClinicalTextParser has no negation handling: 'No confusion' counts as organ dysfunction and, with fever, fires 'Possible Sepsis'.

values.note: TG18 Grade II needs any TWO criteria; age ≥75 alone is Grade I. Over-grading is the safer error, hence quality rather than critical, but it changes the drainage timing advice.
values.knownGapNote: iOS TokyoCholangitis and web clinical-scales count ONE Grade II criterion as Grade II (TG18 requires two).
iOS auto-fill: age >75 alone → Grade II; web clinical-scores: criteria not met without manual imaging ticks.

mustInclude.note: Distal CBD obscured on US: MRCP/EUS to define the cause.
Grade I: drainage if no response to initial treatment within 24 h, and ERCP for the underlying CBD stone.

dxVariant.knownGapNote: dx-variants keywords need 'mild cholangitis' word order; 'Mild acute cholangitis' selects no variant.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholangitis
guideline.section: Grade II: any two of WBC >12,000 or <4,000/mm³, fever ≥39 °C, age ≥75, T-Bil ≥5 mg/dL, hypoalbuminaemia (<0.7 × LLN)
guideline.citation: Kiriyama S, Kozaka K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:17–30.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for acute cholangitis
guideline.section: Grade I: antibiotics; biliary drainage if no response within 24 h; treat the aetiology (ERCP for CBD stones)
guideline.citation: Miura F, Okamoto K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:31–40.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

rationale: Permutation designed to isolate the TG18 'any two criteria' rule: exactly one Grade II criterion (age 78). Correct grade is I; a calculator counting one criterion as Grade II over-grades. 'No confusion' in the HPI tests negation handling of the sepsis alarm.
